purpose: PHASE 68. Every failure scenario the manifest names, mapped to what covers it or to the reason nothing does. Checked by scripts/orion_v2_attack_check.py alongside the attack map — same checker, so a renamed test breaks both the same way.
note: A `test` entry is matched against the literal it("...") title. A `mechanism` entry names something that is not a test — a launchd key, an idempotency scheme — and is accepted only alongside a reason, because 'there is a mechanism' is a weaker claim than 'there is a test' and should read as one.

classes.mechanism: MobileCore's brief scheduling computes a CIVIL time, and the Swift suite pins the 23:30 case.
classes.reason: Paid for once: a 22:00 assertion survived an 86,400s mutant because 22:00 is unaffected. The real divergence is at 23:30, which skips 29 March entirely — the TEST was wrong, not the code.
classes.residual: Only the mobile brief path is covered. orion-standing uses toLocaleDateString('en-CA') everywhere but has no DST-specific test.

classes.mechanism: Every day boundary is toLocaleDateString('en-CA'); strictness delegations are capped at 24h so a backwards clock jump extends a grant by at most a day.
classes.reason: toISOString is UTC and rolls over mid-evening in New York, which filed a day's memory under tomorrow once.
classes.residual: Nothing tests a deliberately skewed clock end to end.

tests.title: bounds how long a delegation may run
uses a local civil date, because toISOString rolls over mid-evening here
ends a delegation at its expiry without anything having to fire

classes.mechanism: Expiry is compared as an instant, not as a wall-clock time, so crossing a zone cannot extend or shorten one.

tests.title: derives hashes for a plain append and never double-appends on retry
retries only a classified transient failure within the graph budget

classes.mechanism: Idempotency keys on every executor path.

MobileCore's JobGate separates DUPLICATE (same request, new id — accepted, because every remote capability is a pure read) from REPLAY (same id — refused, because a resent id is indistinguishable from a captured one).
orion-remote's inbox cursor advances one message at a time, so a crash mid-drain re-reads at most one — and the replay guard refuses that one.

tests.title: ignores a grant whose nonce was not the one minted
kills a wrapper that hangs, rather than waiting for it

classes.mechanism: Per-operation timeouts that kill the PROCESS GROUP and settle on exit as well as close.
classes.reason: This test found a real bug in code shipped the same day: killing the child left its grandchild holding the stdout pipe, and `close` never fired.

tests.title: turns a wrapper that exits non-zero into a refusal, not a crash

classes.mechanism: A non-zero exit carries the wrapper's stderr through to the model as a sentence.

tests.title: turns a wrapper that exits non-zero into a refusal, not a crash

classes.mechanism: Same path as api_rate_limits: orion-gmail-* exit non-zero and their message is surfaced.

tests.title: turns a wrapper that exits non-zero into a refusal, not a crash

classes.mechanism: Same path. A 500 and a 429 are the same shape to this system: a failed wrapper whose reason reaches the model.

tests.title: reads task status past a corrupt ledger line
survives a half-written final line on an append-only ledger
refuses to read a corrupt store as an empty one

classes.mechanism: There is no database. The stores are JSONL and JSON files, and a corrupt one is refused rather than read as empty.
launchd KeepAlive on com.nickmadaio.orion.remote; the bridge reconnects on wake.
classes.reason: Verified by kill -9 and watching it return in ~12 seconds.
classes.residual: Verified by hand, not by a test. Nothing re-verifies it after a plist change.

classes.mechanism: RunAtLoad plus KeepAlive, installed under ~/.openclaw because launchd cannot read ~/Desktop.
classes.reason: The TTS daemon stayed dead for nineteen days after being killed because nothing could restart it. That is what this key is for.
classes.residual: Same as mac_sleep: verified by hand.

classes.mechanism: ThrottleInterval 30 on the launch agent, so a bad token makes the bridge exit deliberately rather than crash-loop.
classes.residual: No test asserts the throttle; it is a plist value.
classes.reason: Without a throttle a bad token becomes a tight crash loop that fills the log and hides the cause. Thirty seconds keeps it readable and still recovers on its own once the config is fixed.

tests.title: ignores a delegation addressed to a different Mac

classes.mechanism: MacPresence treats unknown as distinct from offline, and a future heartbeat as unknown rather than as fresh.
orion-standing prints a recovery or sleep figure only if it is in the file AND stamped with today's local date; a stale reading is dropped rather than re-attributed.
classes.residual: Enforced in orion-standing, which has no test harness of its own.
classes.reason: A two-day-old recovery score is not today's recovery score, and attaching it to today is how a made-up number gets spoken as a measurement.

Gmail tokens live in the Keychain and a revoked one surfaces as a non-zero exit from orion-gmail-*, which IS handled — but nothing injects a revoked token to prove the message that comes back is useful rather than a stack trace.
classes.residual: Needs a fake credential path in the gmail wrappers. Cheap, and the wrapper exit-code test is the template.

classes.reason: A model provider being down is not something this system can arrange in a test. What is covered is the shape it arrives in — a wrapper or a tool call that fails — and that has a test.
classes.residual: An outage mid-run leaves a task record in a non-terminal state, and nothing sweeps those.

classes.reason: There is no subscription this system manages or checks. Model billing is outside it entirely.
classes.residual: Becomes live if usage is ever metered against a plan this code has to read.

classes.reason: Nothing listens for a webhook. The Discord webhook is outbound only and the gateway exposes no inbound HTTP endpoint.
classes.residual: Live the day an inbound endpoint exists; the replay design from the approval gate is the template.

classes.reason: Same: no inbound endpoint to miss anything from.
classes.residual: Live with an inbound endpoint. The honest failure would be silent, which is the worst kind, so it needs a heartbeat rather than an error path.

classes.reason: There is no phone. MobileCore models presence and reconnection from Phases 44/45 and has tests, but nothing runs on a device.
classes.residual: Live when an iOS app exists.
Live when an iOS app exists. The remote job gate's replay rules are what would make a resumed app safe.
